#!/bin/sh

# Flux batch script converted from Slurm
# Note: Flux does not support in-script directives for resource specification
# This script should be submitted with the following command:
# flux batch -N 1 -n 1 -t 2h --setattr=system.memory=4096M --job-name=mcmicro_SMM_multisample --output=mcmicro-{id}.log --cwd=/research/labs/hematology/hemedata/m302618/projects/spatial/cdx_pipeline_mforge/MCMICRO/ script.sh
#
# Resource specifications:
# -N 1         : 1 node (implicit, single task)
# -n 1         : 1 task (implicit from original Slurm script)
# -t 2h        : 2 hour walltime (from --time=2:00:00)
# --setattr=system.memory=4096M : 4GB memory (from --mem=4G)
# --job-name=mcmicro_SMM_multisample : job name (from -J=mcmicro_SMM_multisample)
# --output=mcmicro-{id}.log : stdout/stderr redirection (from -o=mcmicro-%J.log)
# --cwd=<path> : working directory (from --chdir)
#
# Note: Flux uses {id} for job ID instead of %J
# Note: Memory specification syntax may vary by Flux version
# Alternative: --setattr=system.memory=4G or --setattr=system.memory=4294967296

# Original job name: mcmicro_SMM_multisample
# Set at submission: flux batch --job-name=mcmicro_SMM_multisample ...

# Original output file: mcmicro-%J.log
# Set at submission: flux batch --output=mcmicro-{id}.log ...
# Note: In Flux, both stdout and stderr go to the same file by default
# To separate: add --error=mcmicro-{id}.err

# Partition: cpu-short
# Note: Flux does not have partitions in the same way as Slurm
# Queue/partition selection is handled through Flux's scheduling configuration
# Performance impact: Job scheduling depends on site-specific Flux queue policies
# Consult site documentation for equivalent resource pools or queues

# Email notification: howe.michael@mayo.edu (ALL events)
# Note: Flux does not have built-in email notification directives
# Performance impact: User must manually monitor job status or implement external
# monitoring solutions using flux job events, flux watch commands, or wrapper scripts
# Consider creating a wrapper script that uses 'flux job attach' with email notifications
# or monitoring flux job status changes with external tools

# Working directory: /research/labs/hematology/hemedata/m302618/projects/spatial/cdx_pipeline_mforge/MCMICRO/
# Set at submission: flux batch --cwd=<path> ...
# Or set in script with: cd /research/labs/hematology/hemedata/m302618/projects/spatial/cdx_pipeline_mforge/MCMICRO/

# Change to working directory (alternative to --cwd at submission)
cd /research/labs/hematology/hemedata/m302618/projects/spatial/cdx_pipeline_mforge/MCMICRO/

module purge
module load nextflow
module load apptainer

export NXF_APPTAINER_CACHEDIR="/research/labs/hematology/hemedata/m302618/apptainer/containers"

nextflow -C mforge_settings.config run labsyspharm/mcmicro --in 20240112_BR062124_Gonsalves_CD45 -with-report

issues: The script correctly documents that Flux does not support in-script resource directives and provides proper submission command syntax in comments.

The memory attribute syntax '--setattr=system.memory=4096M' may not be correct for all Flux versions. Flux typically does not use the 'system.memory' attribute path. The correct syntax is often '--setattr=system.memory' with just a number (bytes), or resource specification may need to be done differently depending on Flux version. Verify with 'flux batch --help' or local documentation.

The output file placeholder '{id}' should be verified. Flux typically uses '{{id}}' (double braces) or '{{jobid}}' for job ID substitution in output filenames, not single braces '{id}'. This may result in literal '{id}' in the filename instead of the actual job ID.

The '--cwd' option syntax in the documented submission command should be verified. Flux uses '--cwd=<path>' or '-o cwd=<path>' depending on version. The script includes a 'cd' command as a fallback, which is good practice.

The script includes both '--cwd' in the submission command documentation AND a 'cd' command in the script body. This is redundant but harmless - the 'cd' will execute even if '--cwd' was used at submission. Consider removing one for clarity.

Memory specification alternatives are mentioned (4G, 4294967296) but the actual Flux memory attribute format should be verified. Standard Flux resource specification may require different syntax like '-o per-resource.memory=4G' or similar depending on version.

No explicit core/CPU count is specified. While '-n 1' specifies 1 task, the number of cores per task is not defined. If the nextflow pipeline uses multiple threads, consider adding '-c <cores>' to the submission command.
The time specification '-t 2h' is correct Flux syntax for 2 hours.
The job name 'mcmicro_SMM_multisample' appears valid (no special characters that would cause issues).
Consider adding error checking after the 'cd' command to ensure the directory change was successful before running nextflow: 'cd ... || exit 1'
The nextflow command may spawn additional processes. Ensure the resource allocation (1 task, 4GB memory) is sufficient for the entire pipeline, not just the parent nextflow process.
